title: Frequently Asked Questions
description: Answers about Peer Support Groups and how Badger Supports works.

items.a: Badger Supports is not a therapy or crisis organization. Our programs, including Peer Support Groups, provide a safe, peer-led space that empowers students to support one another and connect with resources. Peer Facilitators are trained in peer support, but they are not licensed counselors.

items.q: Is Badger Supports only for UW-Madison Students?
items.a: Yes. Our programs are open to undergraduate, graduate, and professional students, including all student identity groups.

items.q: Are Peer Support Groups only for students with mental illnesses?
items.a: Peer Support Groups are open to all students, because we believe everyone can benefit from building a supportive community. Even if you’re not seeking support right now, showing up for a fellow Badger—or learning how to offer support with confidence and compassion—helps break the stigma, anxiety, and stress surrounding mental health.

items.q: How many students are usually in a group?
items.a: Peer Support Groups usually consist of 5-10 students.

items.q: When and where do Weekly Groups meet?
items.a: Peer Support Groups are drop-in and commitment-free, making it easy to drop in when it works for you! All groups are held in the Student Mental Health Hub (Rm. 3203 in the Student Activity Center).

items.q: What is Badger Supports’ official email?
a: Our primary email is directors@badgersupports.org. Communications may also be sent to hello@badgersupports.org.
Staff & volunteers may use their personal @wisc.edu email addresses for communications. View contact information on our team roster.

items.q: How can I get involved as a leader?
items.a: You can learn more on our Get Involved page! If you have specific questions not covered there, please don’t hesitate to contact us at hello@badgersupports.org.

items.q: What does dual registration with UHS-Prevention mean for Badger Supports?
a: Badger Supports is proud to have a dual-registration advising relationship with University Health Services - Prevention at UW-Madison.

This advising partnership reflects our shared commitment to strengthening peer-to-peer mental health support on campus. As part of this partnership, UHS-Prevention staff advise our student team to ensure our student-created training reflects accurate information and best practices.

We do not represent or speak on behalf of UHS-Prevention unless explicitly stated. Badger Supports is an independent Registered Student Organization; and all organizational decisions are made by students.

items.q: Are you affiliated with The Support Network?
items.a: No. Badger Supports has no affiliation with any national organization.

blocks.title: Seeing a question not answered?
blocks.body: Reach out at hello@badgersupports.org. On Wisconsin!
